transcript: I've been a little bit down about musical theater recently, but this week I got a glimpse into the future, and let me tell you, it's looking bright. I got invited to the National Alliance of Musical Theaters Festival of New Musicals, something I have dreamed of attending for years. Every year, NAP brings together eight exciting new musicals, each presenting 45 minutes of their show to producers and theaters around the country, hopefully finding their next home and getting further development. Shows like Come From Away and The Drowsy Chaperone and Thoroughly Modern Millie all got their start at now. Unfortunately for me, we are in the middle of election season and my job is a little bit wild right now, so I only got to go to one day of the festival and only got to see three shows, but oh, my goodness, it was a dream. My first show of the festival was Fouad of Nazareth. This was written by Fouad Dakwar about his experience of growing up as a Palestinian American who as a teenager dreamed of becoming a rock star. And the summer his parents sent him to Palestine to go to. I love what we saw. It's very much a funny, light hearted comedy, but also obviously touches on some very important topics. This needs to be produced immediately. I need to see the whole thing. My next presentation was the Ramayana by Manik Chosik. This was based on an ancient Indian epic and It compared its cultural significance and, like, scale to something like Star Wars. It's been told and retold for thousands of years. It's gods and monsters, romance and exile. And it's being adapted into three concept albums. So we got a little musical mixtape with an insane cast, including Koo Koo Verma, who I love. This was very, very much my thing. Kind of had a little Hadestown vibes. I want to hear it all immediately. And then maybe my most anticipated was bloodline A hip hop odyssey by Fermin Suero, Jr. And Pete white. I'm a little bit obsessed with the creative team, not gonna lie. I heard some of their music over the summer at the festival, but getting to see it in context was everything. This is a hip hop reimagining of the Odyssey. We're talking Odysseus and his journey home, cyclopses and gods and shipwrecks, and, of course, his wife Penelope, back home raising their son and fighting off suitors. The music is so good, I've literally had it stuck in my head ever since. Plus, they had a crazy cast, including Evan Rachel Wood and Christina Pitts. I need it immediately. Three very different shows, different styles, massive creative swings. And there were five more I didn't even get to see. This is why I love theater so much. There are so many incredible stories waiting to be told with so many brilliant, creative, talented people bringing them to life. I will absolutely be following All of these creative teams. I cannot wait to see what's next for all of these shows. Thank you, nampt. See you next year.
classificationReason: Creator attended the NAMT Festival of New Musicals and saw three shows (including 'Fouad of Nazareth'). No single show is the primary focus, and none of the mentioned shows appear on the provided list. Qualifies as a roundup of 3+ shows.
